title: Asiana Airlines Flight 214: automation-mode awareness, airspeed monitoring, stabilized approach, and evacuation survival surface
summary: Asiana 214 is encoded as a flight-deck automation and monitoring case: approach path, autothrottle/flight-mode understanding, airspeed monitoring, go-around timing, training/documentation, and survival/evacuation surfaces are separated.

status_history.note: Added as rev0027 flight-deck state / CRM rail lane record.

place.location: San Francisco International Airport, California, United States

claims.claim: The NTSB page identifies Asiana 214 as a July 6, 2013 Boeing 777 accident at San Francisco in which the aircraft struck the seawall, with three passenger fatalities, serious injuries, and a postcrash fire.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The NTSB sequence summary records a visual approach, high glidepath, FLCH SPD selection, A/T HOLD mode not noticed by the crew, and multiple unstabilized-approach indications before impact.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The NTSB probable-cause and contributing-factors summary includes mismanagement of the approach, unintended deactivation of automatic airspeed control, inadequate airspeed monitoring, delayed go-around, automation complexity/training/documentation, nonstandard communication/coordination, and supervision/fatigue issues.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The NTSB survival-factors summary records that about 98 percent of occupants self-evacuated and 99 percent survived, keeping evacuation/survivability as a separate surface from approach-causal analysis.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

type_payload.system: Boeing 777 approach automation / autothrottle mode / flight crew monitoring / evacuation response
sequence_of_events: Visual approach with glidepath and speed-management anomalies; automation mode/state divergence not corrected; airspeed decayed; delayed go-around; impact short of runway and postcrash evacuation.
type_payload.proximate_cause: unstabilized approach and inadequate airspeed control/monitoring before impact
contributing_factors: automation mode complexity and training/documentation limits
latent_conditions: automation mode knowledge did not translate into decisive shared state
training and documentation surfaces require correction tracking
survival factors need separate child record to avoid causal conflation

handling_notes: Aviation records must preserve the dignity of passengers, crew, families, responders, and survivors.
Do not flatten human-factors findings into pilot blame; separate physical system state, displayed state, automation mode, training, procedures, supervision, fatigue, and investigation/legal status.
This is historical/evidentiary infrastructure, not operational flight-safety guidance or legal advice.

unknowns: The record uses NTSB page extracts rather than full report second-pass; detailed recommendation closure and simulator/training history remain open.
next_actions: Second-pass extract NTSB full report and recommendation closure.
Compare with other automation-mode cases, including China Airlines 140, Turkish 1951, and Qantas 32 for controls.
